original_value: AbstractStories of cyber attacks are becoming a routine in which cyber attackers show new levels of intention by sophisticated attacks on networks. Unfortunately, cybercriminals have figured out profitable business models and they take advantage of the online anonymity. A serious situation that needs to improve for networks’ defenders. Therefore, a paradigm shift is essential to the effectiveness of current techniques and practices. Since the majority of cyber incidents are human enabled, this shift requires expanding research to underexplored areas such as behavioral aspects of cybersecurity. It is more vital to focus on social and behavioral issues to improve the current situation. This paper is an effort to provide a review of relevant theories and principles, and gives insights including an interdisciplinary framework that combines behavioral cybersecurity, human factors, and modeling and simulation.

result.paraphrase: Abstract: Cyber attacks are increasingly routine, with attackers demonstrating higher levels of intent through sophisticated network attacks. Unfortunately, cybercriminals have developed lucrative business models and exploit online anonymity, creating a serious challenge for network defenders. As a result, a paradigm shift is needed to make current techniques and practices more effective. Because most cyber incidents are human-enabled, this shift must broaden research into underexplored areas such as the behavioral side of cybersecurity. Greater emphasis on social and behavioral factors is essential to improving the current situation. This paper reviews relevant theories and principles and offers insights, including an interdisciplinary framework that integrates behavioral cybersecurity, human factors, and modeling and simulation.
